relevance_note: The paper reports a family with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant ('Whole-exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous c.A1939C (NM_001270508) p.T647P variant in TNFAIP3') and a second family with 'the p.N98Tfs25 TNFAIP3 variant'.
method_note: Read the whole paper (a JACI letter with an online-repository Methods section and Table E1) and transcribed values by hand into a Python builder script; a second script checked every span verbatim against the paper Markdown and every row against the schema field list. Table E1 has the patient as a column; its column header is 'Subject III.1 (reference range)'. Individuals: family 1 (Fig 1 pedigree, no family label) III.1 proband, III.2 younger sister, II.2 mother, II.4 (died at 17 of early-onset SLE; relationship to the proband, sex and genotype not stated, so no variant row); family 2 (Fig 2 I, no family label) a 4-year-old boy labelled here by the paper's description '4-year-old nonconsanguineous white male' (also called 'the patient', 'this boy', 'The additional case of HA20'), and his symptomatic father. Subject II.1 is mentioned only as a 'family member' whose serum was used for cytokine measurement, with no clinical or genetic information, so no row was made for II.1. Not recorded as values: inheritance for III.1/III.2 (the mother II.2 carries the variant and the pedigree 'shows segregation', but the paper never states maternal inheritance) and for the boy (father carries it); this is in parental_testing_statement instead. III.1 age: presented as an '8-year-old', with follow-up '24 months later' after baricitinib, so age at last evaluation is not stated; individual-level age at onset left 'not reported' because the earliest symptom (choreoretinitis from 6 months) was attributed at the time to congenital infection; the 6-month onset is kept on that feature row. Variant notation printed non-standard ('c.A1939C', unversioned 'NM_001270508', 'p.N98Tfs25'); recorded as printed. Variant type not stated by the authors for either variant. The boy is not called proband/index, so is_proband is null. n_patients_reported is null: the authors give no total (they name 'affected patients (subjects III.1, III.2, and II.2)' plus the boy and his father). The panel reference E1 (Omoyinmi 2017) is cited for the sequencing panel used for the boy; the paper does not say he was described there, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null. Table E1 laboratory values outside the printed reference ranges (hemoglobin '10 g/L (120-160 g/L)', raised IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, low ALP) were not turned into phenotype rows because the paper does not call them abnormal. The NOD2 testing in the laboratory sentence has no result stated, and no non-TNFAIP3 variant is attributed to anyone. Group-level statements (cytokines higher 'in heterozygotes for p.T647P'; p65 and IRF3 in 'all heterozygotes') were used only in functional_evidence_statement, not as phenotypes. The father's 'similar clinical features' were not mapped to checklist items. The boy's 'recurrent oral inflammation' was not taken as oral ulcers; III.1's 'no history of systemic symptoms' was not taken to exclude fever. Contradictions in the paper: (1) the text places III.1's lesions in the paracentral lobule and thalamus 'on the left', but the Fig 1 legend says 'right paracentral lobule'; (2) the text says STAT1/STAT3 phosphorylation was raised in lymphocytes 'from subject III.1', the Fig 2 D-E legend says 'from p.T647P TNFAIP3 heterozygotes'; (3) minor P-value differences between text and Fig E2 legend (IRF3 .0043 vs .004; STAT1 .037 vs .03).

study_type.span: We report a case of TNFAIP3-mediated autoinflammation manifesting as progressive neuroinflammation.

treatment_summary.value: Empiric anti-tuberculosis treatment (isoniazid/rifampicin/pyrazinamide/moxifloxacin); prednisolone 2 mg/kg/d weaning to 0.5 mg/kg/d plus mycophenolate mofetil (no response); intravenous cyclophosphamide (6 doses) with prednisolone at 2 mg/kg/d (poor response); baricitinib 6 mg/d (oral JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor) with rapid clinical and radiologic improvement; prednisolone weaned off
span: empiric anti-tuberculosis treatment was started (isoniazid/rifampicin/pyrazinamide/moxifloxacin)
she received treatment with 2 mg/kg/d prednisolone, weaning to 0.5 mg/kg/d over 6 months and mycophenolate mofetil (1200 mg/m^2/d). There was no response to this treatment
Intravenous cyclophosphamide (6 doses, 500-750 mg/m^2) was then given, and prednisolone continued at a higher dose (2 mg/kg/d). There was poor response to these treatments
was started on baricitinib (6 mg/d), an oral JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor that blocks interferon signaling

This resulted in rapid clinical and radiologic improvement: 24 months later, she remains stable, with no further seizures and marked resolution of the intracerebral inflammatory lesion (Fig 1, H-J). Prednisolone was weaned off for the first time in 2 years.
